BiblicalUsage: The word speaks of collapsing under a weight, whether the body or the heart. David cries that he is feeble and sore broken, roaring by reason of the disquietness of his heart, and the psalms return again and again to bones broken and a spirit broken before God. Yet the same brokenness becomes an offering: the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, and a broken and contrite heart He will not despise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God does not waste our breaking. He hears the cry of the crushed, and the heart that collapses before Him is the very sacrifice He accepts.
